notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped (1 Uno, 1 breadboard, 6 LEDs, 6 x 220 ohm resistors, 13 jumper wires).

Each LED has its own 220 ohm series resistor between its Uno pin and the LED anode; cathodes go via short black wires to the top negative rail, which the Uno GND wire feeds. LEDs on pins 7,6,5,4,3,2 in order left to right.

Breadboard coordinates are read from the image. The image's top half is rows j-f (LEDs and resistor tops) and its lower half is rows e-a; these are mapped to catalogue banks 'b' (rows f-j) and 't' (rows a-e). LED anode columns 7,10,13,16,19,22; cathode columns 8,11,14,17,20,23. Each resistor spans the centre gap from row f (bank b) to row e (bank t) in its anode column; the blue wire lands at row c of the same column.
Exact rail hole numbers (tn.1 for the Uno GND wire, tn.8/11/14/17/20/23 for the black wires) are approximate; all tn holes are one strip so the connectivity is unaffected.
Uno GND pin is the GND next to pin 13 on the digital header; it is mapped to GND.1 (all Uno GNDs are common).
The array in the code only changes the order the LEDs are lit in software, not the wiring.
